unmapped_findings: Fe-15Al (15 at.% Al) has an A2 bcc disordered matrix up to the melting temperature (b0012).
Fe-15Al is a binary reference alloy with no MC carbides or Laves phase; Table 1 lists only polygonal grains (500 μm) and no precipitates or dendrites (b0015, figure_001).

For Fe-15Al, yield stress in compression (356 MPa) is higher than in tension (344 MPa), i.e. tension-compression asymmetry, which is related to glide of screw dislocations with nonplanar (delocalised) core, the Bauschinger effect and notch sensitivity (b0029, b0033).
Binary Fe-15Al fractured transgranularly with very fine cleavage facets and has the highest room-temperature ductility (16%) among the investigated alloys (b0035, figure_004).
At elevated temperatures, Fe-15Al shows no yield-stress anomaly; its compressive yield stress decreases gradually and monotonously with increasing temperature (b0038, figure_005).
